decisions.statement: The rows are read from beside the page of the command that wrote them.
The page of the command running a change or an apply is read.
Where that page sits is read from the index.
Every numbered file of a page's rows is read rather than the first alone.
A numbered file that is not there is no file left unread.
A row a write left half appended is passed over and the rest of the file read.
The file that row is in is named beneath the table under its own heading.
The runs are gathered under what ran rather than under the page read.
A window is chosen by the rule the check measuring chooses one by.
A count of runs names the most recent runs.
A period names every row stamped within that period.
The rows are drawn by the rule the check measuring draws its rows by.
A row naming the change phase or the apply phase is read and no other row is.
The row a command run wrote beside the same page counts nowhere here.
A change's ceilings are read from the page of the change that ran.
A change stating no processor ceiling is drawn with the one every change is held to.
An apply is no change page and is drawn with no ceiling.

definition: what the runs of a change and of an apply cost, read back over a window
